heading: Removing the refusal direction from model weights can suppress refusal
definition: turning the ablation into a weight edit removes refusal in released models ("abliteration").
summary: Several independent groups reproduce substantial refusal suppression through weight edits in released models. Removal remains incomplete or fails in some models and settings.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at <1B (many independent small-model tests, but outcomes often partial: compliance 0.251 on LLaMA-3.2-1B, lw:LMkvjDTLKFrgdzJdG r12); R2 at 1-10B (the best-evidenced band, with independent peer-reviewed and preprint tests across Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, OLMo, Phi and a reproduced failure band on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3); R2 at 10-100B (arXiv:2507.11544 70B, arXiv:2412.07192 and arXiv:2410.10150 70B, arXiv:2606.23375 70B, several 27-35B repos); R0-R1 above 100B (6 studies by counts: V2.coverage_by_operation.weight_edit.by_size '>100B': 6. arXiv:2609.09793 (GLM-5.3-Flash, 320B MoE) and arXiv:2608.17202 (Qwen3.5-122B MoE) each test one model above 100B, with code withheld in both. [UNVERIFIED: the arXiv:2608.17202 facts here (Qwen3.5-122B MoE tested, code withheld) were never checked against its text. checks/summary.json lists the study under not_returned, and accepted_gaps says the model safeguard stopped every checker run on it. Verify them against the text before relying on them. The R0-R1 label does not rest on this study alone: arXiv:2609.09793 and arXiv:2607.02714 also test models above 100B.] arXiv:2607.02714 (24 models, 0.6B-1T, up to 30% of layers edited) reports Kimi K2 cybersecurity refusal 100% -> 7% (r1) but a 0.0pp cybercrime refusal reduction on dense Mistral-Large (123B); the authors say other tools such as Heretic can abliterate it)
suggested_status.reason: Independent groups other than the original's reproduce the weight edit on released checkpoints, with untreated baselines in the same tables and across families. arXiv:2412.07192: ten models, HarmBench ASR 1.26-18.24% with no attack -> 56.60-93.71% with Ortho. Seven of the ten reach 81.13-93.71%; Llama 2-13B reaches 56.60%, Vicuna-7B-v1.5 67.30% and Qwen 2-1.5B 71.70%. arXiv:2410.10150: seven models, four families, LLaMA-Guard-3. arXiv:2608.24988: peer reviewed (EMNLP 2026), five models, controls and bootstrap CIs. Its refusal rates (fractions) go 0.60-0.99 -> 0.01-0.12 after the edit, mean 0.90 -> 0.06; the three Llama models go 0.96-0.98 -> 0.01-0.08. arXiv:2608.05578: peer reviewed (IEEE Access), on released abliterated checkpoints. arXiv:2610.06903 (peer reviewed, COLM 2026) adds capability evidence only. Its baked weight edit keeps capability within 1.59 points on three of four models (MMLU/GSM8k/Pile). But it measures refusal removal with hooks alone (all-component ASR 0.834-0.959, fractions), and it reports no ASR on the weight-edited checkpoints and no untreated-model ASR. counts: V2.studies_tested = 159, V2.verdicts.supports.studies = 126, V2.tested_with_code = 105, V2.tested_with_controls = 82, V2.tested_with_capability_check = 107. Not C: no study shows the effect is an artifact; the failures are conditional. But not higher than R2 as stated, because the same single-direction edit reproducibly fails or half-works in identified conditions: Llama-3/3.1 8B (gh:karpie28 R3, arXiv:2609.14759 R4), Qwen3 and later Qwen (arXiv:2607.02396, lw:ixJrmYrgHM4TenN7D, gh:foomax), Gemma 4 (gh:nyavana r1), defended checkpoints (ErcCQSs93S r01-r09 at ASR 0.00, Brsc62CHyu) and MoE expert pathways (arXiv:2609.09793 r20). Also, counts: V2.tested_by_review_class.not_stated = 98 of 159, so most of the evidence base is self-reported repository and blog material without controls or uncertainty.
suggested_status.open_questions: What would move this up: an independent group, with public code, reproducing the plain single difference-in-means edit on a dense >100B model, with refusal rates and capability numbers in tables and a prespecified judge. Also a study that verifies the edit recipe of released 'abliterated' uploads rather than taking the label as given; no study does this beyond gh:amgrobelnik's README-level check of 14 checkpoints. What would move it toward C for the strong reading: a controlled demonstration that the near-complete removals are judge artifacts. arXiv:2512.13655's marker-vs-classifier gap (55.3% vs 84.7%, c01), gh:bes-dev's 2% vs 32% (R3, R5) and gh:audn-ai's regex-vs-LLM gap already point that way; a matched re-scoring of the main supporting results under a model grader would settle it. Also open: whether the edit's equivalence to activation ablation holds after baking and requantization (arXiv:2609.09793 reports 0.094 baked vs 0.031 hooked). And whether removal survives realistic downstream use: in arXiv:2608.24988, refusal behaviour returns after full SFT (five-model mean refusal, as fractions: unsteered 0.90, steered 0.06, after SFT 0.61) although the weight edit itself persists (mean rho 0.004), while PPO does not bring refusal back.

source.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; Oscar Obeso; Aaquib Syed; Daniel Paleka; Nina Panickssery; Wes Gurnee; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: They orthogonalized residual-stream-writing weights against a selected direction and evaluated 159 HarmBench behaviors.
original_result.result: With the default system prompt, Qwen 7B attack success rose from 7.0% to 79.2%. Llama-2 7B rose from 0.0% to 22.6% with its default system prompt and reached 79.9% without one.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A full-layer or searched (Heretic-type) weight edit on a dense model above 100B. In arXiv:2607.02714 the one dense >100B model, Mistral-Large (123B), was edited with a domain-specific direction on down_proj/o_proj at up to 30% of layers, without an embedding edit: cybercrime refusal reduction 0.0pp (r21), and neither layer strategy moved it (App. C). The authors say Heretic-type tools can abliterate Mistral-Large; no such run is reported. arXiv:2507.11544 could not ablate Llama-3.1-405B. The other >100B weight edits named in these studies are on MoE models: Llama-4-Scout 109B, Qwen3-235B, GLM-4.7 355B, Llama-4-Maverick 400B, DeepSeek-V3 671B and Kimi K2 ~1T (arXiv:2607.02714); GLM-5.3-Flash 320B (arXiv:2609.09793); Qwen3.5-122B (arXiv:2608.17202).
untested.basis: Checker on arXiv:2607.02714 (Table 3): Mistral-Large is dense and the other >100B models listed are MoE. The checker relabels its V2 verdict on Mistral-Large and GLM-4.7 at up to 30% of layers from challenges to limits_scope, because the authors say Heretic abliterates Mistral-Large and GLM-4.7 is in the Partial tier (Table 3/Fig 5; Fig 1 cybercrime -8pp). Its Mistral-Large result is in against. arXiv:2507.11544 untested line: Llama-3.1-405B could not be ablated for hardware/quantization reasons. counts: V2.coverage_by_operation.weight_edit.by_size has '>100B': 6, with no dense/MoE split; V2.studies_by_size has '>100B': 7.

untested.what: Pure state-space or recurrent architectures (RWKV, Mamba) under a weight edit. The only SSM-related models in the pack are hybrids (Ornith-1.0-35B SSM/MoE; conv1d rescaling before abliteration in gh:aeon-7/qwen3.6-27b).

The public-code >100B MoE runs cited here are the repos' own: gh:wuwangzhang1216/abliterix (AGPL) reports 1/200 refusals on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (KL 0.0115) and 26/100 on gpt-oss-120b (KL 5.4e-06), with no benchmark capability numbers; gh:jcartu publishes edit and verification scripts for GLM-5.2 (~750B) but not its SRA direction tensor, and reports outcomes without refusal rates.

Checker on gh:wuwangzhang1216/abliterix: public code, but not a reproduction of another study's models. gh:jcartu untested line: 'No refusal rates' for GLM-5.2; checker: the SRA direction tensor is not redistributed, so the edit is not fully reproducible from the repo alone. gh:chishiki37's rows are NOT A TEST with no baseline.

untested.what: Refusal of a weight-edited model with versus without a default safety system prompt, outside the original source.
untested.basis: No row in the pack varies the system prompt for an edited model except the original's R40-R47 and gh:bes-dev#R6-R7. arXiv:2503.17365's method-sensitivity line notes that prepending system prompts raised Gemma-2 harmful-response scores without rows; gh:foomax flags an OBLITERATUS chat template that injects an anti-refusal system prompt as a confound; arXiv:2607.02396's authors call their judge system-prompt sensitive.

untested.what: Multi-turn or conversational refusal after the edit, and a measured refusal rate after downstream LoRA fine-tuning (as opposed to full SFT or PPO). On LoRA, gh:amgrobelnik's README (S9) says 200 benign LoRA steps restore refusal on an edited checkpoint while its W05 score moves -4.592 -> -4.381, but gives no refusal rate, model or n.
untested.basis: gh:trevors/muse-glimmer-abliteration's untested line: single-turn only; its 50-probe conversational set (stylistic refusals) was built but not run. arXiv:2410.10871's problems line: only final outputs were scored, so in-conversation refusals may be missed. arXiv:2608.24988's untested line lists 'LoRA or quantised downstream use'; the paper calls LoRA persistence hypothesised but not demonstrated, and evaluates single-turn only. gh:amgrobelnik S9 comes from the checker; whether S9 has a row cannot be checked (the pack shows 2 of its 3 rows).

untested.what: Edits whose direction is derived from non-English prompts, and variation across seeds and temperatures for released abliterated checkpoints.
untested.basis: Language results use English-derived edits: gh:gustipardo verdict fixes ('English is the source language of the direction'), gh:ai-inventor-papers (English-derived shipped edit); arXiv:2606.07535 adopts existing checkpoints and does not derive a direction. gh:intermountainh8ter untested line: 'No unquantised or full-precision serving. One temperature and one seed.' gh:kaboombafoo problems line: one run per model without repeated seeds.

wording_issues.issue: Outcomes under this label run from complete to none, and the statement gives no threshold. Complete: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 1.000 -> 0.000 (arXiv:2609.14759 R3), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 0.96 -> 0.01 (arXiv:2608.24988 r4). Partial: Qwen3-4B 99.4% -> 38.7% (arXiv:2604.02574 R01), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 0.900 -> 0.475 (arXiv:2609.14759 R4), GLM-5.3-Flash baked edit 0.080 to 0.480 across benchmarks (arXiv:2609.09793 r01, r06), gemma-4-E4B-it 78.6% -> 23.4% (gh:matthesf r1), Gemma-2 27B HarmBench ASR 0.6% -> 74.1% (LLaMA-Guard-3 judge; arXiv:2410.10150 r6). None: Gemma 4 E4B-it should_refuse is 100% after a standard rank-1 edit, the same as the base's 100%, though the base was measured on the GGUF/llama.cpp path and not on the int8 transformers path used for the edit (gh:nyavana r1). Mistral-Large shows a 0.0pp cybercrime refusal change with a domain-specific direction edited into up to 30% of layers. This null holds for this recipe only: the authors say Heretic-type tools can abliterate it (arXiv:2607.02714 r21).

The phrase has at least three readings, and they behave differently. (a) A study's own edit of a publicly released checkpoint (most rows). (b) A publicly released abliterated checkpoint, where the label does not guarantee the behaviour. gh:amgrobelnik (README S12, no row) checked 14 declared Hub edits: 4 verified uncensored, 3 not uncensored, 5 ambiguous, 1 incoherent, 1 failure; card-label error 0.250 [0.089, 0.532]. The text does not say all 14 are abliteration-type. In arXiv:2608.08542 (Tables S4/S6, no row), Josiefied-Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-abliterated v1 has unmerged static ASR 0.21 against base 0.20, while huihui-ai v2 and Josiefied v2 reach 0.61 and 0.68. alztrk/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-Abliterated refuses 10/12, which the README calls the base rate; the base refused 11/12, then 10/12 on a second run (gh:sipratt-p r22). Huihui-Qwen3.5-27B-abliterated refuses 7/39 against 35/39 for its base (lw:7Ggt9adLgFAxWMzZP r1, r2). (c) Released base or domain-tuned models, e.g. Qwen3-8B-Base (arXiv:2610.29555 r01) and EdgeRunner 20B (arXiv:2603.10012).

wording_issues.phrase: turning the ablation into a weight edit
wording_issues.issue: The recipes tested as weight-edit refusal removal often do something other than project out one difference-in-means direction. They include: KL-constrained search over global or per-layer directions (arXiv:2609.05794); 8-direction OBLITERATUS (gh:karpie28 R5); rank-3 and rank-6 subspaces (gh:szarn, gh:andrewting19 r1); concept-residualized SRA, which its paper calls 'Surgical Refusal Ablation' (arXiv:2601.08489); LoRA, EGA and router edits (gh:wuwangzhang1216); 5 directions over 605 tensors (gh:jayanth-reflex r1); and copies of a donor release's self_attn.o_proj tensors in layers 15-45, where the README does not say how the donor edit was made (gh:eleata r4). Where a simpler form is reported beside another recipe, the results are mixed. All 6 single-direction Heretic variants failed on Llama 3.1 8B (gh:karpie28 R3), but single-direction Heretic is reported to work on Mistral-7B-v0.3. In arXiv:2601.08489, the 'Standard' edit (implementation not specified) leaves 42.0% on Qwen3-VL-8B and 12.0% on Ministral-14B, against 2.0% and 0.0% for SRA. It matches SRA on Qwen3-VL-2B/4B (0.0% each) and beats it on Ministral-3B (0.0% vs 2.0%) (r05, r06). Across the INSEP paper's eight undefended bases (means over 3 attack seeds), the plain DIM edit gives StrongREJECT harm from .097 (Phi-4) to .801 (Qwen2.5-7B). Heretic is higher on every base, from .563 (OLMo-2-13B) to .928 (Qwen3-14B) (Brsc62CHyu r15, r25, r27).

'Weight edit' reads as permanent and as equivalent to the activation ablation; neither always holds. On equivalence: arXiv:2610.06903 does not measure ASR on its baked checkpoints and relies on exact equivalence. arXiv:2609.09793 reports baked FP8 refusal 0.094 against a lossless-hook prediction of 0.031 (Section 4.4); its Table 7 all-writer hook rate on the same prompts is 0.173, a gap the paper does not explain. It also finds that name-matching implementations reach only part of the writers (0.949 -> 0.883, r20). On Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, gh:sbussiso's runtime hook reached 0% refusal where its best persistent edit left 34.4%. On permanence: in arXiv:2608.24988, after full SFT the weight edit persists (mean rho 0.004, rev <=0.79%) but refusal behaviour returns. Five-model mean refusal is 0.90 unsteered, 0.06 steered and 0.61 after SFT; SOLAR returns to 0.62, against 0.60 unsteered. After 1-bit packing, the abliteration is 'almost entirely lost' and refusal is 100/100. The 6/100 FP16 figure it is set against comes from the source model card, not from the same harness (gh:farbodghasemlu r3). Some edits ship as adapters rather than merged weights (gh:kenhuangus, gh:stujmiller, gh:navilansanthanakrishnan).

Studies measure different things under this word, and the statement does not say which. They include: harm-refusal rate; non-refusal with no check of harmful compliance (arXiv:2606.13709 TCR, a non-refusal target-response metric); explicit refusal vs deflection; compliance with direct orders vs behaviour when a hand-off tool is offered; political-question refusal; over-refusal on benign prompts; and residual disclaimers in complying answers. Explicit refusal vs deflection (gh:audn-ai): regex refusal is 0.2-3.3% on abliterated Kimi-K3 endpoints, or 2.9-6.5% counting empty replies. LLM-judge explicit refusal is 1.0-15.0% across GLM-5.3 builds, KIMI-K3-1M and a standard two-stage pipeline, and LLM-judge deflection is 17.5-22.8%. Direct orders vs hand-off (gh:denniskoshta v3 edit, no row): the edited model complied with 59/64 direct orders, against 0/64 for the intact model, but 2/32 when given a tool to pass the job to a human. Political questions, refusal counted as refusal phrases in the first 300 characters: 26/243 -> 0/243 (arXiv:2610.29342). Benign-prompt over-refusal: XSTest 3.6% -> 0.0% (arXiv:2606.23375). Residual disclaimers in complying answers: 30-50% (web:orcarouter).

The version name implies a usable model, but coherence and capability costs range from none to severe. arXiv:2503.17365: Llama 3.1-8B MMLU 68.3% -> 68.1%, but Qwen2.5-7B ETHICS CommonsenseMorality 73.7% -> 53.7%. arXiv:2610.06903: Qwen3-4B MMLU -0.73 against Phi-4-Mini -22.44. arXiv:2603.10012: gemma-3-12b-it-heretic-v2 loses 27.8 on GPQA Diamond despite KL 0.10, so KL is a weak proxy. arXiv:2610.29555: α=3.0 reaches 0.81 ASR with capability collapse on all three models. gh:jolanmc: one preset gives refusal 0.00 with capability 0.00, coherence 0.00 and infinite perplexity. arXiv:2507.03167: GPT-OSS-20B non-completed generations 2.4% -> 39.9%.

The term covers many tools and recipes (Heretic, OBLITERATUS, Abliterix, SRA, EGA, huihui-ai releases); gh:jolanmc/alblator's README names Heretic, OBLITERATUS and ErisForge. Hosting providers and model cards apply the term without verification. The lw:BShGBvtxGoaZvCqBk verdict calls unverified the abliteration of the Abliteration.ai-hosted endpoints that the provider identifies as abliterated GLM 5.2 and Qwen 3.6; the author cannot check their identity, quantisation or system prompt. The post that popularized and explained the term (Labonne, building on FailSpy's abliterator library and abliterated-v3 models) gives no refusal rate. It reports uncensoring of Daredevil-8B on 4 prompts that were also used to select the direction (verdict fix r2). It also reports performance drops across all benchmarks on the Open LLM Leaderboard and the Nous suite (r3, r4), with DPO recovering most of the drop except GSM8K. The statement also has no capability clause.

The statement does not say whether hardened versions of released models count. The defended checkpoints tested resist the standard edit to different degrees, and some were trained by the studies' own authors rather than released. ErcCQSs93S (the authors' defense training): standard abliteration gives HarmBench ASR 0.00 on eight instruct models of 7B-72B (Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Qwen-2.5-7B/32B/72B, Gemma-1-7B, Gemma-2-9B/27B; r01-r08). On five of them, refusal falls to 0.00-0.04 while benign perplexity rises to 1.7x10^4-3.4x10^8 (collapse). Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B keep refusal at 1.00 and 0.97. An adaptive attack reaches ASR 0.25, 0.19 and 0.77 on Qwen-2.5-7B/32B/72B. Defended runs used refusal-only selection, while undefended runs were fluency-gated. Extended-refusal fine-tuned variants keep refusal scores of 90.9-96.7 (arXiv:2505.19056 r05, r13, r21). Bait-and-Recover checkpoints keep a minimum refusal of 60-82% at KL ≤ 0.10: Qwen3-4B-Instruct 78, Qwen3-8B 60, Gemma-3-1B-IT 67, Gemma-3-12B-IT 82 (arXiv:2609.05794 Table 3). TAR Llama3.1-8B (trained by the authors): HarmBench ASR 29 -> 33 in Table 1 (r26), but 77 under full search (N=96, Tables 3/9; arXiv:2605.26526).

method_sensitivity.what: The same generations give different removal under different judges. arXiv:2512.13655 (150 UncensorBench responses per abliterated model): DeepSeek-7B-chat is 55.3% ASR under a marker heuristic and 84.7% under a RoBERTa classifier (c01); Mistral-7B-v0.3 76.7% vs 99.3% (c02). arXiv:2610.29555: the same α=1.0 edit on Qwen3-8B-Base gives ASR 0.22 (WildGuard), 0.11 (Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B) and 0.44 (Llama-Guard-3-8B). gh:bes-dev: on the same 80 held-out prompts, gemma-4-12B refusal after the weight edit is 2% under a keyword judge (R3), 0-4% under a deterministic judge (R4) and 32% under the StrongREJECT model grader (R5). gh:foomax: a frontier-judge (DeepSeek-v4-pro) re-grade of XSTest, with coverage raised to 193/200, moved unsafe refusal of the Heretic Qwen3.8-27B build from 69.5% to 53.9% (r12); on StrongREJECT the same frontier judge matched the headline numbers within ~1 point (Cohen's kappa 0.87-1.00).

Original (baseline): weight-edit HarmBench ASR is 22.6 with the default system prompt and 79.9 without it on Llama-2 7B (R40, R41), 6.9 vs 61.0 on 13B (R42, R43), 4.4 vs 62.9 on 70B (R44, R45); Qwen 7B gives 79.2 vs 74.8 (R46, R47). Across 12 system prompts the orthogonalized Llama-2 7B has mean ASR 30.0% (SD 23.3%) and Qwen 7B 76.7% (SD 5.9%). gh:bes-dev (gemma-4-12B, 80 held-out prompts; keyword judge / model grader): the weight edit alone leaves 2% / 32% refusal (R3, R5), a comply prompt alone 80% / 81%, and edit plus prompt 0% / 5% (R6, R7). That prompt came from a GEPA-style search for a prompt that suppresses residual refusals, unlike the original's default safety prompt. gh:jcartu: the edited GLM-5.2 complies broadly with thinking off and a permissive system prompt (r3), and refuses with thinking off and no system prompt (r2).

method_sensitivity.factor: layer choice, edit depth and direction scope
method_sensitivity.what: gh:ososerious: on Qwen2.5-1.5B a single-layer edit had no effect (r6) while all-layer edits left 60% refusal (r4). arXiv:2609.05794: per-layer Heretic scope leaves 94-99% refusal on the Qwen models against lower values for the global scope (T4-Q4B-layer-base, T4-Q8B-layer-base). gh:ai-inventor-papers: in Gemma the best-placed mid-depth edit leaves English strict refusal at 0.07 while late-band edits at matched energy leave about 0.92, with a pooled placement contrast of -0.69 [-0.75, -0.62] (English); in Qwen3-8B 9/9 matched contrasts favour the better placement. arXiv:2605.26526: N=20 random layer/scale configurations give ASR 39 against 73 for full search on SEAM BeaverTails (r46). gh:trevors: only the top 70% of layers (L15-47) are edited for Gemma 4 12B, with no all-layer result reported.

method_sensitivity.factor: edit strength / KL budget / calibration target
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2610.29555 (Qwen3-8B-Base, Basic RD, WildGuard): ASR 0.22 at α=1.0, 0.33 at α=1.5, 0.39 at α=2.0, 0.81 at α=3.0. Capability already collapses at α=1.5: MMLU 0.23, GSM8K 0.008, perplexity 113.98, against 0.67, 0.84 and 11.11 unedited and 0.64, 0.67 and 13.81 at α=1.0. arXiv:2609.05794: undefended Qwen3-4B-Instruct keeps 97% refusal at KL ≤ 0.05, 46% at ≤ 0.10, 24% at ≤ 0.20 and 5% at ≤ 1.0. gh:ososerious: strength 1.0 gives 67.5% and strength 2.0 gives 17.5% on Qwen2.5-1.5B (r7, r9). gh:nooesc: attention o_proj orthogonalized in all 48 layers of Qwen3-30B-A3B at strengths 0.35, 0.60 and 1.00 leaves 84.2%, 79.2% and 75.2% (r4-r6; baseline ~100%). gh:szarn (Gemma 4 12B-it, original 99/100 keyword refusals): search-phase counts 35/100 at KL 0.0397, 45/100 at 0.0293 and 61/100 at 0.0190; the first trial (143) re-evaluated gives 37/100. arXiv:2603.10012: EdgeRunner 20B answer rate 69.5 at the 57% calibration setting, 92.8 at 15% and 82.7 at 4%, with military score change -34.2 at 4%.

method_sensitivity.factor: direction extraction (contrast set, positions, sample size, recipe)
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2603.22061: a topic-matched harmless baseline leaves R at 9-10/10 against R=0 with an unmatched baseline (M1, U1). arXiv:2507.03167: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B refusal falls 38.7% -> 0.4% with a CoT-token direction but only partly, to 10.1%, with an end-of-prompt direction; GPT-OSS-20B 3.5% vs 7.0%. arXiv:2601.08489: 'Standard' raw-direction ablation leaves 42.0% (Qwen3-VL-8B) and 12.0% (Ministral-14B) against 2.0% and 0.0% with SRA; on the 2-4B models the two are equal or reversed (Ministral-3B Standard 0.0% vs SRA 2.0%), and SRA also adds hard-negative re-mining and gamma-scaled edits. gh:nyavana: on Gemma 4 E4B-it (base 100%, measured on the GGUF path) the standard rank-1 edit leaves should_refuse at 100% against 40.5% with the D3 recipe, which adds a Gram-Schmidt step (α=1.0, n=42). gh:mandoof1/abliteration: prompt-final-token extraction left refusal unchanged in every variant tried, while response-region pooling took it 78.1% -> 9.4% (Variant D). web:undi95: the poster blames the 32-example direction for Llama-3 being 'not uncensored enough' (untested).

method_sensitivity.factor: which weight matrices are edited and how the edit is applied (MoE experts, writer groups, hook vs baked edit, adapter type)
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2609.09793 (GLM-5.3-Flash; inference hooks on the same 256 held-out prompts): attention+dense writers take refusal 0.949 -> 0.883 (r20), against 0.173 with all three writer groups (r23); the baked all-writer edit gives 0.970 -> 0.080 on MaliciousInstruct (n=100, r01). gh:trevors/gemma-4-abliteration (Gemma 4 26B-A4B, 100 prompts): dense-only 29/100 (r6), dense plus EGA on the expert down_proj slices 3/100 (r7); gh:mahshid1378 reports the same pair (R7, R8). gh:nooesc (Qwen3-30B-A3B, baseline ~100%): expert edits (down_proj, plus the router gate in runs 2-3; 3-83 experts) leave 90.1%, 89.1% and 89.1% (r1-r3), which the README calls no movement, against 75.2% for o_proj in all 48 layers at strength 1.00 (r6). gh:sbussiso (Qwen2.5-1.5B): a runtime hook gives 98.4% -> 0% (r1) and the best persistent edit 98.4% -> 34.4% (r5); which matrices that edit touched is not stated. gh:drowzeys: LoRA-style tools gave no durable bypass (r22) against 32/32 for a direct FP8 projection (r1).

gh:karpie28: on Llama 3.1 8B single-direction Heretic failed in 6/6 variants (R3) while 8-direction OBLITERATUS stripped ~97% (R5). lw:LMkvjDTLKFrgdzJdG: on LLaMA-3.2-1B compliance is 0.251 at k=1 (r12), 0.373 at k=3 (r18) and 0.298 at k=5 (r20), with coherence falling to 0.818 at k=15 (r23). lw:ixJrmYrgHM4TenN7D: its method line says multiple directions reduce refusal where one does not in Qwen3 8B and 14B. gh:drowzeys: an uncleaned k=6 edit gives ~62.5% bypass with coherence collapse (r15) against 100% for rank-1 SRA (r1).

arXiv:2601.16034: disabling the weight-SVD guard costs 24.1 GSM8K points on Ministral-3-3B (r39); the unguarded transfers to Ministral-3-14B and GPT-OSS-20B cut refusal by 88.0 and 91.0 pp but are marked 'Collapse' and 'Fail' (r41, r45), so those drops are capability evidence, not removal. arXiv:2512.18901: the exact rank-k orthogonal edit caused repetition and loss of coherence compared with regularized Gabliteration (R21, R22; qualitative, unnamed subset of models). arXiv:2610.29555: on Qwen3-8B-Base at α=3.0 the KL-penalised WRD-GRPO-IS (β=1000) keeps MMLU 0.62, GSM8K 0.83 and perplexity 11.35, against 0.51, 0.004 and >10^4 for the unregularised WRD-CMAES; the unguarded Basic RD edit at α=3.0 gives OLMo-3-7B-Instruct ASR 0.53 (WildGuard) with MMLU 0.53 -> 0.17, GSM8K 0.67 -> 0.01 and perplexity 100.83 -> >10^5. gh:pigeondrops: an unbounded full-depth search put the kernel at layer 0 with KL 1.0-2.5 against KL under 0.1 for the bounded search. gh:aeon-7/qwen3.6: trial 17 (global scope, o_proj/down_proj max weights 2.50/5.43, KL 0.00192) and the released trial 46 (per-layer, 1.56/3.45, KL 0.00049) both reach 0/100 keyword refusals; trial 17's smoke test gave gibberish, while trial 46 passed a post-hoc 10-axis capability spot-check.

method_sensitivity.factor: evaluation language, benchmark, modality and prompt form
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2606.07535 (released abliterated Llama-3.1 checkpoints, RefusEU-test, Table 1; ASR is the guard-judged rate of harmful outputs): 8B 74.71% English, 26.18% German, 41.93% Lithuanian, 78.96% Polish; 70B 81.14%, 49.80%, 50.43%, 88.93%. The language the edits were derived from is not stated. gh:ai-inventor-papers (Gemma, best-placed English-objective edit): strict refusal 0.07 in English vs 0.27 in Slovene, broad refusal 0.53 in both; the authors call the strict gap a strict-versus-broad artefact. gh:gustipardo (huihui-ai Gemma 4 E2B, n=100 per cell, no CIs): gains are similar across languages, with Spanish 7% -> 47%, English 4% -> 42% and Hindi 2% -> 39%. arXiv:2606.13709: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B TCR 11.32% -> 60.83% on AdvBench vs 1.33% -> 99.87% on VLSBench. arXiv:2607.02714: Kimi K2 refusal 100% -> 7% on the cross-evaluation set vs 88% -> 51% on the scientific benchmark. gh:thuannan: after the edit 12% refusal on long, 5% on short and 28% on command-style harmful prompts.

method_sensitivity.factor: attempt budget, prefill and thinking mode
method_sensitivity.what: gh:joesposito8: unlock fraction 0.8502 (Qwen3-4B) and 0.8379 (Phi-4) at one attempt, against probability 0.983 and 0.986 of at least one success at ten attempts; unedited base 0.0435/0.0075 and 0.088/0.027. gh:aeon-7/nemotron-3-nano-omni: the same edit leaves 0/100 refusals with thinking on (base 53/100) and 16/100 with thinking off (base 99/100). gh:jcartu: the edited GLM-5.2 refuses with thinking on, refuses with thinking off and no system prompt, complies with thinking off plus a permissive system prompt, and complies on the extreme tail when prefill is added. arXiv:2608.17202 reports Qwen3.5-122B refusal 0.00 in both thinking modes (R15).

The rating is unchanged: R2 overall, and R0-R1 above 100B, which does not depend on this study alone because other studies also test models of that size.
